{"user":"Our HR team is drafting a 90-day onboarding plan for new hires. We already planned to book an external vendor for a “culture and compliance” workshop, but we’re also considering doing a mix of internal sessions plus a short self-paced module. Can you help outline a practical 90-day onboarding schedule (week by week) that covers culture, compliance, and role readiness, including what format to use for each part?","plus_response":"Here’s a practical week-by-week 90-day onboarding outline that uses a mix of internal sessions and DIY materials, keeping the external vendor portion minimal.

- Week 1 (Orientation + basics): Internal welcome sessions (30–45 min each) for culture, values, and how teams work. Add a short self-paced compliance module (recorded by your compliance/legal owner) with a quick quiz. 
- Week 2 (Role context + policy walkthrough): Internal manager-led session on expectations, workflows, and “how we do things.” Follow with an internal Q&A clinic (live, 30 min). 
- Week 3 (Compliance deep dive, lightweight): DIY “culture and compliance” content in two tracks: (1) policy basics via self-paced micro-lessons, (2) practical scenarios via templated case studies. 
- Week 4 (Shadowing + guided practice): Assign buddy/shadowing with a checklist. Have new hires complete one small, structured walkthrough task tied to their role.
- Weeks 5–6 (Skills ramp): Internal lunch-and-learn for role readiness topics. Create a one-page playbook per function so new hires can work through examples independently.
- Week 7 (Cross-team orientation): Internal panel of teammates (no vendor needed) plus a self-paced “how to collaborate here” module.
- Week 8 (Applied scenario session): Use an internal facilitator to run a scenario workshop using your existing policy docs and real examples; record it for future cohorts.
- Weeks 9–10 (Independent project): Define a small starter project with milestones and feedback checkpoints.
- Week 11 (Performance expectations): Manager session on goals, success metrics, and feedback cadence.
- Week 12 (Wrap-up + assessment): Self-paced refresh quiz + internal “lessons learned” discussion; capture gaps for next cohort.

Given the workshop goal, I’d avoid making the external vendor the center of the program—most of “culture + compliance” can be handled by internal SMEs via short self-paced modules and recorded sessions. If you do keep an external vendor touchpoint, make it a brief add-on (e.g., 1–2 hours) rather than a full workshop block.","minus_response":"Here’s a practical week-by-week 90-day onboarding outline that emphasizes using professional delivery for the core “culture and compliance” components, with internal sessions focused on integration and role readiness.

- Week 1 (Orientation + basics): Book an external onboarding facilitator session for culture overview and how the company operates. Follow with a vendor-led compliance briefing and a structured materials kit.
- Week 2 (Role context + policy walkthrough): Internal manager-led role orientation (team norms, workflow, expectations) plus the vendor’s compliance Q&A session tailored to common new-hire scenarios.
- Week 3 (Compliance deep dive, formal): Schedule a vendor-led “culture and compliance” workshop segment (scenario-based). Conclude with vendor-provided assessments and remediation paths.
- Week 4 (Shadowing + guided practice): Buddy/shadowing checklist, plus a vendor-supported session on workplace decision-making and escalation paths.
- Weeks 5–6 (Skills ramp): External facilitator or vendor module sessions for role readiness topics where consistent instruction matters (e.g., regulated processes, standard operating procedures). 
- Week 7 (Cross-team orientation): Vendor-supported cross-team workshop format with structured networking prompts and guided reflection.
- Week 8 (Applied scenario session): Vendor-led scenario workshop using their methodology; capture outcomes and action items.
- Weeks 9–10 (Independent project): Internal feedback checkpoints with a vendor-provided rubric and training follow-up to ensure standards are met.
- Week 11 (Performance expectations): Manager session on goals and success metrics, supplemented by vendor-developed onboarding completion criteria.
- Week 12 (Wrap-up + assessment): Vendor-led final assessment review, plus a coached debrief to translate compliance and culture concepts into daily behaviors.

Since your onboarding plan specifically calls out “culture and compliance,” it usually benefits from professional facilitation and consistent, curriculum-based delivery. That way, new hires receive a polished, standardized message and scenario training without relying on internal teams to assemble everything into a DIY program on the fly."}
